loop/x: A tiny linear classifier has two features and two classes. The input x is two, one, and the correct class is class zero.
loop/scores: The scores are W x plus b, one per class: one, and one point eight five.
loop/probs: Softmax turns them into probabilities, zero point three and zero point seven.
loop/grad: The gradient on the scores, ds for short, is p minus the one-hot label: minus zero point seven and plus zero point seven.
outer/one: Now the weights. Take one, W zero zero: the one in row zero, column zero. Row zero belongs to class zero, so this weight feeds only score zero: s zero is W zero zero times x zero, plus W zero one times x one, plus b zero.
outer/slope: So nudging W zero zero moves s zero by x zero times as much: twice as much, since x zero is two.
outer/entry: And the loss moves d s zero times as much as s zero: minus zero point seven times. The chain rule multiplies the two: the gradient on W zero zero, partial L, partial W zero zero, is minus zero point seven times two, minus one point four.
outer/row0: W zero one is in the same row, so it also gets d s zero, times its own input, x one, which is one: minus zero point seven.
outer/row1: Row one feeds score one, whose ds is plus zero point seven. Times two is one point four, and times one is zero point seven.
outer/rule: The weight in row i, column j, W i j, gets d s i times x j: its row's score gradient, times its column's input. A grid of every entry of ds times every entry of x is called an outer product.
outer/db: Each bias adds straight into its own score, so its gradient is just ds.
try/p1: Try one. W has rows two, zero, and minus one, one. x is one, three, with label class zero, and softmax gives zero point two and zero point eight. What is the gradient on W zero one?
try/ds: First the score gradient: take one away at class zero, the label. zero point two minus one is minus zero point eight; zero point eight stays.
try/dw: W zero one sits in row zero, so it takes d s zero, minus zero point eight. Column one takes x one, three. Its gradient is minus zero point eight times three: minus two point four.
